The Latest column is the newest commit only; the failure tables below keep each suite's last result. Click a GPU to show or hide its test steps; a GPU with failures opens on its own. A step that shows ⊘ or – for several pushes is a blind spot: the GPU's verdict cannot see it.

New failures: tests that passed on the previous push and fail now

A test is new when it failed on this push and passed on the previous push that ran it (for a GPU test, the same step on the same GPU). Pushes where it was skipped, or hit a setup or build failure, do not count. On its next result it moves to Known, keeping the push it first failed at. The last column checks the scheduled GPU run of the same commit: a failure it reproduces is real, one it does not is a flake candidate.

Smart trigger: which GPU types each run tested

all 32 of 31 of 3none (build skipped too)

The select job picks the GPU types (H100, B200, MI350) whose code a change touches. PR and push runs should skip the rest; a "GPU suite" is one GPU type's tests in one run. Scheduled and manual runs must test all three. A fallback means the changed paths were unavailable, so every suite ran.

GPU hours and runs per day, by run outcome

passedtest failurebuild failuresetup failurecancelled

GPU hours

Runs

GPU hours are job start-to-finish time on GPU runners, all triggers. Setup failures and cancelled runs are spent GPU time that produced no test result. A build failure stops the run before its GPU jobs, so it shows in runs, not hours. Runs count only runs that used GPU time or failed the build.

GPU minutes per run

pushPRmedian per day

Push and PR runs that passed or failed tests. Cancelled runs and setup or build failures stopped early and are left out. Hover a day for the 25th and 75th percentiles. A PR run tests only the GPUs its paths touch, so the spread mixes one-GPU and all-GPU runs.

Queue time: waiting for a GPU runner (minutes)

B200H100MI350median per day (per hour, in the 3-day range)

Time from a GPU job being queued to a runner picking it up, all triggers, jobs that ran. Each line is the day's median (the hour's, in the 3-day range); hover for the 25th and 75th percentiles. "Last to finish" is how often that GPU's job was the last one on a PR run: that job decides when the PR gets its result, so its queue is the wait the queue tile reports.

GPU jobs running at once

B200H100MI350peak per day (per hour, in the 3-day range)

The most GPU jobs of each type running at the same moment, from job start and finish times; hover for the time-weighted average and the most jobs waiting for a runner. Every branch and trigger counts, since they share the runners. Only this repository's CI workflows are counted: other repositories share some runner pools, so a flat peak with jobs waiting means the pool is full, not that demand stopped.

Job duration (minutes)

The slowest 10% shows stalls the median hides, such as a wheel download that stalls.

Slowest tests, main pushes (seconds)

From pytest's --durations list in each GPU test job of a push to main: each step prints only its 25 slowest test phases (setup, call or teardown), so "Runs" counts how often a test was among them. A test's time is the sum of its listed phases. Ranked by median time.
